Some matchers are too loose for your tests. `toBeTruthy()` passes for `1`, `"no"` and `[]`, so it doesn't prove that a value is `true`. This rule reports the matchers and modifiers you list.

Without options it doesn't report anything.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"vitest/no-restricted-matchers" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Both examples use `{ "toBeTruthy": "Use toBe(true) instead" }`.

Reported:

{/* bad {"options": [{"toBeTruthy": "Use toBe(true) instead"}]} */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "vitest";

test("a new user is active", () => {
  const user = { active: true };
  expect(user.active).toBeTruthy();
});
```

Not reported:

{/* good {"options": [{"toBeTruthy": "Use toBe(true) instead"}]} */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "vitest";

test("a new user is active", () => {
  const user = { active: true };
  expect(user.active).toBe(true);
});
```

## Options

The rule takes one object. Each key is the chain you write after `expect(..)`, joined with dots. Each value is a hint shown with the report, or `null` for no hint.

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "vitest/no-restricted-matchers": [
      "error",
      {
        "toBeTruthy": "Use toBe(true) instead",
        "not.toHaveBeenCalledWith": null,
        "resolves": "Await the promise, then check the value"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Key | What it reports |
| --- | --- |
| A matcher, such as `"toBe"` | `expect(a).toBe(b)`, but not `expect(a).not.toBe(b)`. |
| A chain, such as `"not.toBe"` | `expect(a).not.toBe(b)`, but not `expect(a).toBe(b)`. |
| `"not"`, `"resolves"`, `"rejects"`, or a chain that ends in `.not`, such as `"resolves.not"` | Every chain that starts with it. |

A matcher must be the whole chain, so `"toBe"` allows this:

{/* good {"options": [{"toBe": null}]} */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "vitest";

test("ids differ", () => {
  expect(createId()).not.toBe(createId());
});
```

A modifier matches whatever comes after it:

{/* bad {"options": [{"resolves": null}], "count": 2} */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "vitest";

test("loads the user", async () => {
  await expect(loadUser(1)).resolves.toEqual({ id: 1 });
  await expect(loadUser(2)).resolves.not.toBeNull();
});
```
